items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: John Kirby Curved (PHONETIC), oh, even Milt Hinton. Well, they all give me something

ctx.x: Right. Well, with Sonny Rollins Robbins, at that time, perhaps it was his nervousness, too, but you have to remember what you accomplished musically, which people constantly are saying. Like David Baker talks about he teaches people what you have contributed to the music. Maybe we could talk about different styles of bass playing and different peoples' contributions, because it's not clear to the average person.
Oh, yeah, well, like I said, I came out of the mold of Blanton and Israel Crosby (PROPHETIC) and a few

others -- Truck Chuck Parham (PHONETIC), John Kirby Curved (PHONETIC), oh, even Milt Hinton. Well, they all give me something, you know, with which to grow. I noticed the younger bassists, you hardly hear them mention the great bassists like Paul Chambers, you know, or Ray Brown, for that matter. Most of the young bassists don't say nothing. They hardly say anything about Oscar Pettiford. But most all the youngsters, I can tell that they followed Paul. Paul was the master. He was the master with the bow, but it…
